#SciOTD 𝗧𝗬𝗣𝗛𝗢𝗢𝗡 𝗠𝗜𝗟𝗘𝗡𝗬𝗢 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗦𝗢𝗨𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗡 𝗟𝗨𝗭𝗢𝗡

On this day in 2006, Typhoon #MilenyoPH (#Xangsane) crossed Southern Luzon and caused widespread damage, flooding, and casualties, even in Metro Manila. Many people considered this the worst typhoon to directly impact Metro Manila since Super Typhoon Rosing in 1995.

Tropical Cyclone MILENYO (international name: XANGSANE) was first spotted over the Philippine Sea east of Visayas on 25 September 2006. The still-developing cyclone intensified quite fast and became a strong typhoon with sustained winds of up to 160 km/h near the center as it approached Samar provinces just two days later. By 27 September, Milenyo first unleashed its fury over the northern part of Eastern Visayas as it grazed Northern Samar before making its first landfall in Sorsogon and crossing the Bicol Region throughout the evening.

The next morning, Milenyo reached CALABARZON and hovered over the southern part of Metro Manila around noontime before heading towards Bataan and the West Philippine Sea by evening. Its eye was observed in the cities of Muntinlupa, Las Piñas, and Parañaque, marked by nearly an hour of silence and relatively clear skies surrounded by an eyewall of thunderstorms.

Along its path, Milenyo showed how destructive typhoons could be: several electric and communication lines were downed, resulting in almost two weeks of power interruptions even in Metro Manila, many crops and trees were either removed of leaves or brought down by violent winds, many structures and houses were either totally destroyed, left roofless, or damaged. This typhoon also brought the attention of the government to the dangers of billboards during typhoons, as it brought down many billboards across Metro Manila, resulting in several deaths.

Due to widespread damage, several areas in Metro Manila, CALABARZON, Bicol Region, Western Visayas, and Eastern Visayas, were placed under State of Calamity after the typhoon. NDCC reported at least 213 deaths, 660 injuries, 48 missing, and affected more than 4.1 million people. It also left more than 6.6 billion pesos worth of damage.
